rationale:
Split into two children. The first reuses an already-accepted declaration and adds no DAG node; the second is one new lemma.

(i) weight_blowup = Submission.frt_weight_blowup_tendsto is step 2 of the supplied proof. It is already comparator-accepted in branch root.first_rectifiability-a1 (status accepted, candidate b951e87) with exactly this frozen type, so the sharing rule lets it be reused verbatim. This is reuse of a finished node, not solving another DAG node. The controller (_existing_lean_name_problem and the child-id mapping in _recursive_lean/runtime.py) maps the child to the existing node and provisions no new worker. The parent therefore need not re-prove the blow-up computation.

(ii) plane_eq_of_integral_eq (new: Submission.allard_tc_tpd_plane_eq_of_integral_eq) is step 5. It is a genuinely reusable fact: an n-plane is determined by H^n⌞plane tested against C_c. Isolating it also fixes a defect in the supplied step 5. That step relies on SimonGMT Grassmannian.eq_of_plane_eq, which lives in Chapter08/ConstancyTangent.lean and is not reachable from import GMT.Ch08.Submission (lake env lean reports "Unknown constant" for it and for projectionLinearMap_eq_starProjection). The child's proof replaces it by Mathlib's isSymmetricProjection_iff_eq_coe_starProjection_range together with Grassmannian.toMatrix_projectionLinearMap.

Steps 1, 3 and 4 stay in the parent. They are short computations local to this statement, and the node budget is tight (127 of max_nodes 200 used, 80 nodes still decomposing):
- step 1: densityRatio(s•y, s·r) = densityRatio(y, r);
- step 3: μ_C.map(s⁻¹•) = s^n μ_C, hence W_{s•y}(s·t) = W_y(t);
- step 4: composition with t ↦ s·t and uniqueness of limits.

How the children give the parent, following the supplied proof (checked in Lean):
- θ' = θ (step 1). The sibling allard_tc_tangent_plane_density gives HasDensity n C.weight y (ofReal θ) and HasDensity n C.weight (s•y) (ofReal θ'). smul_closedBall' and the homogeneity hypothesis at A = B_r(y) give densityRatio(s•y, s·r) = densityRatio(y, r) for r > 0, after cancelling ofReal(s)^n with ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left. Compose with r ↦ s·r, which maps 𝓝[>]0 into 𝓝[>]0, and apply tendsto_nhds_unique: ofReal θ' = ofReal θ, so θ' = θ.
- Blow-up identity (step 3). For g ∈ C_c and t > 0, μ_C.map(s⁻¹•) = ofReal(s)^n • μ_C, by Measure.ext with preimage s•A. Then integral_map and integral_smul_measure give (s·t)⁻¹^n ∫ g((s·t)⁻¹(z − s•y)) dμ_C = t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹(z − y)) dμ_C.
- Equal plane integrals (step 4). Apply weight_blowup at (y, T, θ), and at (s•y, T', θ') composed with t ↦ s·t. With the identity, uniqueness of limits and cancellation of θ = θ' > 0, this gives ∫_T g dH^n = ∫_{T'} g dH^n for every g.
- T' = T: plane_eq_of_integral_eq.

subproblems.title: Weight blow-ups at a tangent point (Ch. 8, Def. 1.1 tested with f(y,S) = g(y))
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, V an n-varifold on U (Varifold N n U), x ∈ ℝ^N, T ∈ G(N,n) and θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ (Simon Ch. 8, Def. 1.1). Then for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), t^{-n} ∫ g(t^{-1}(z − x)) dμ_V(z) → θ ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n as t ↓ 0, where μ_V = V.weight and H^n = μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → ∀ g : C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ t⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ z, g (t⁻¹ • (z - x)) ∂V.weight) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (θ * ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), g y ∂μHE[n]))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Shared accepted declaration. This child is exactly DAG node root.first_rectifiability-a1.weight_blowup-a1 (Lean Submission.frt_weight_blowup_tendsto, comparator-accepted at candidate commit b951e87c9540d60a4b82361e9d286261aaf2579b, identical frozen type); in the selected proof it is step 2 ("Weight blow-ups"), used with U = univ, V = C at (x, T, θ) = (y, T, θ) and at (s•y, T', θ'). Its accepted proof, reproduced verbatim:

Source: Step (0b) of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 (Definition 1.1 tested with functions that do not depend on the plane variable). Notation: μ := V.weight = V.measure.map Prod.fst; G := Grassmannian N n; for t ∈ ℝ let φ_t : ℝ^N × G → ℝ^N × G, φ_t(z) := (t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x), z.2), so that rescaledMeasure V x t = ENNReal.ofReal (t⁻¹ ^ n) • V.measure.map φ_t; ι_T(y) := (y, T), so that planeVarifoldMeasure T = (μHE[n].restrict T.plane).map ι_T.

1. Test function. G is compact (instance Grassmannian.instCompactSpace, SimonGMT Chapter08/Varifold.lean:271). Define f : ℝ^N × G → ℝ by f(y, S) := g(y). Then f = g ∘ Prod.fst is continuous, and support f ⊆ (support g) ×ˢ univ, so tsupport f ⊆ (tsupport g) ×ˢ univ, which is compact as a product of two compact sets. Hence f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ).

2. By the third clause of HasTangentPlane V x T θ applied to f: ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) → θ · ∫ f d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) as t → 0 within (0, ∞).

3. Plane side. ι_T is continuous, hence measurable, and f is continuous, hence strongly measurable; by integral_map, ∫ f d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) = ∫ f(y, T) d(μHE[n].restrict T.plane)(y) = ∫_{T.plane} g dμHE[n].

4. Rescaled side. Fix t > 0. By integral_smul_measure, ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) = (ENNReal.ofReal (t⁻¹ ^ n)).toReal · ∫ f d(V.measure.map φ_t), and (ENNReal.ofReal (t⁻¹ ^ n)).toReal = t⁻¹ ^ n because t⁻¹ ^ n ≥ 0. The map φ_t is continuous, so integral_map gives ∫ f d(V.measure.map φ_t) = ∫ f(φ_t z) dV.measure(z) = ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) dV.measure(z). Applying integral_map once more, to the measurable map Prod.fst and the continuous function y ↦ g(t⁻¹ • (y − x)): ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z.1 − x)) dV.measure(z) = ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) d(V.measure.map Prod.fst)(y) = ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) dμ(y). (integral_map only needs a.e.-measurability of the map and a.e.-strong measurability of the integrand; no integrability is used, so the identities hold even if some integral is the Bochner value 0.)

5. Conclusion. By 4, for every t > 0, t⁻¹ ^ n · ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ(z) = ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t). Since Set.Ioi 0 ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, the two functions of t are eventually equal along 𝓝[>] 0, so (Filter.Tendsto.congr') by 2 and 3 the left side tends to θ · ∫_{T.plane} g dμHE[n]. ∎
proof_key_steps: f(y,S) := g(y) belongs to C_c(ℝ^N × G) because G is compact.
Apply the convergence clause of HasTangentPlane to f.
∫ f dv(T) = ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n by integral_map along y ↦ (y,T).
For t > 0, ∫ f dV_{x,t} = t^{-n} ∫ g(t^{-1}(z − x)) dμ_V by integral_smul_measure and integral_map (twice).
Transfer the limit by eventual equality on (0,∞).

subproblems.title: An n-plane is determined by the H^n-integrals of C_c functions over it
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and T, T' ∈ G(N,n). Here G(N,n) = Grassmannian N n consists of the symmetric idempotent real N×N matrices of trace n, and S.plane is the range of the orthogonal projection represented by S. Let H^n = μHE[n] be the n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N. If ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n = ∫_{T'.plane} g dH^n for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), then T' = T.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (T T' : Grassmannian N n), (∀ g : C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ), ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), g y ∂μHE[n] = ∫ y in (T'.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), g y ∂μHE[n]) → T' = T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof ("T' = T"), i.e. the plane half of the printed "Θ^n(μ_C, λy) = Θ^n(μ_C, y) (by 5.3)" step in the proof of Simon 8.5.7. Correction: the parent cites SimonGMT Grassmannian.eq_of_plane_eq, but that lemma (Chapter08/ConstancyTangent.lean) is not reachable from import GMT.Ch08.Submission ("Unknown constant"). Steps 5–6 below replace it by an argument that uses only imported lemmas.

Notation. H := μHE[n], a measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N. For a set P, H⌞P := H.restrict P, so ∫ y in P, g y ∂H is by definition ∫ g d(H⌞P). For S ∈ G(N,n) = Grassmannian N n, let p_S := S.projectionLinearMap. This is the linear map ℝ^N → ℝ^N whose matrix in the standard orthonormal basis is S.1, and S.plane = range p_S by definition.

1. Dimensions. By Grassmannian.finrank_plane, finrank ℝ T.plane = n and finrank ℝ T'.plane = n.

2. Regularity. By step 1 and SimonGMT Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule (for a subspace P with finrank P = n, H⌞P is regular), H⌞T.plane and H⌞T'.plane are regular measures on ℝ^N.

3. Riesz uniqueness. ℝ^N is a Hausdorff, locally compact space with its Borel σ-algebra. Let g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ). The hypothesis, read right to left, gives ∫ g d(H⌞T'.plane) = ∫ g d(H⌞T.plane). By Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported, two regular measures with equal integrals against every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) are equal. Its regularity instances come from step 2. Hence H⌞T'.plane = H⌞T.plane.

4. Supports. By SimonGMT Chapter03.support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule, the support of H⌞P is exactly P whenever finrank P = n. With step 1 and step 3, as subsets of ℝ^N,
 T'.plane = support(H⌞T'.plane) = support(H⌞T.plane) = T.plane.
Submodules with equal underlying sets are equal (SetLike.ext'), so T'.plane = T.plane as submodules.

5. A Grassmannian point is its orthogonal projection. Let S ∈ G(N,n).
 - p_S ∘ p_S = p_S (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_comp_self).
 - p_S is symmetric (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric).
 So p_S is a symmetric projection. By Mathlib LinearMap.isSymmetricProjection_iff_eq_coe_starProjection_range, it equals the orthogonal projection onto its range: p_S = (range p_S).starProjection = S.plane.starProjection, as linear maps. Also, by Grassmannian.toMatrix_projectionLinearMap, LinearMap.toMatrix b b p_S = S.1, where b is the standard orthonormal basis (Grassmannian.coordinateBasis).

6. Conclusion. Apply step 5 to S = T' and S = T, and use step 4:
 T'.1 = toMatrix(p_{T'}) = toMatrix(T'.plane.starProjection) = toMatrix(T.plane.starProjection) = toMatrix(p_T) = T.1.
G(N,n) is a subtype of N×N real matrices, so T' = T (Subtype.ext). ∎
proof_key_steps: finrank T.plane = finrank T'.plane = n, so H^n⌞T.plane and H^n⌞T'.plane are regular (SimonGMT regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule).
Equal C_c integrals of two regular measures force H^n⌞T'.plane = H^n⌞T.plane (Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported).
The support of H^n⌞P is P (support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), so T'.plane = T.plane.

Each p_S is a symmetric idempotent, hence p_S = S.plane.starProjection (isSymmetricProjection_iff_eq_coe_starProjection_range). Its coordinate matrix is S.1 (toMatrix_projectionLinearMap), so T'.1 = T.1 and T' = T.
